key_insight: The paper shows that narrowing the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is impossible under common similarity assumptions, and that only a stronger combination of assumptions yields a better time bound.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this clarifies when asynchronous training can or cannot achieve homogeneous-like speedups across workers with different data sources.
method: Proves impossibility results under first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone is still insufficient.
Introduces strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition to derive an improved time complexity bound.
evidence_signal: The evidence is theoretical: the abstract reports proof-based complexity comparisons rather than experiments or empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The improved guarantee relies on stronger assumptions than weak interpolation, so applicability may be limited when real worker data are highly non-identical.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
